title: Unsupervised Automated Policy Overrides
pattern: Implementing automated incident response mechanisms that have unsupervised permissions to disable, relax, or clear security protections (like ACLs or rate limits) during system overload or failure.
why_bad: An attacker can intentionally trigger the anomaly (e.g., launching a targeted traffic spike) to force the automation to disable safety mechanisms, creating a self-inflicted authorization bypass window.
detection: Automatic error recovery methods that execute command line calls deleting access lists, firewall parameters, or security policies.
fix: Constrain automation: utilize a change budget that limits the magnitude and scope of automated policy changes, requiring manual human validation once exhausted.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 8, p. 158.
